legacy_root.question: Do Chinese, Japanese, Russian, German or Korean technical sources describe orchestration or deliberation mechanisms that have no English-language equivalent in this program's corpus - and is any of them implementable from the source as written?

register.claim: Japanese 稟議 is sequential written circulation: a staffer without decision authority drafts a 稟議書, related offices stamp in series, then a 決裁権者 ratifies. 差し戻し/却下 are named. This is not P19 rfc-last-call (simultaneous last-call) and not P18 two-key-dual-control (parallel keys).
register.implementability_note: Named roles (drafter, approvers, ratifier), a document object, sequential stamps, and reject/return. Compilable as a DAG.
register.mechanism: 稟議制 / 稟議書 circulation
register.original_language_quote: 担当者が簡易案件を作成して関係者に回し、それぞれに同意のための捺印と承認を求めることをいう。
register.secondary_quote: 個人の権限では決定することができない事柄について、関係者の承認を経て最終的な決裁を得るためのプロセス
register.translation: Ringi means having the person in charge draft a simple matter, circulate it to the relevant people, and seek each person's seal and approval.

register.claim: 根回し is obtaining prior consent from stakeholders before the formal act. The captured Wikipedia entry gives no roles, document, or stopping rule. Absent from English protocol slugs, but not implementable from the source as written.
register.implementability_note: Metaphor plus slang. No procedure to compile.
register.original_language_quote: 物事を行う際に事前に関係者からの了承を得ておくこと
register.secondary_quote: 物事を行う際に事前に関係者からの了承を得ておくこと
register.translation: Obtaining the consent of the people concerned in advance when doing something.

register.claim: PRC 合议庭: odd-n collegiate bench, majority decides, minority opinion must be written into the (non-public) minutes. Hung outcomes are avoided by odd n. Inverse of P17 jury-with-allowed-hung; not P56 minority-report-mandatory (that report is a public council product).
register.implementability_note: Odd-n membership, majority rule, mandatory minority minute, signatures: a compiler can emit that protocol from the text.
register.mechanism: 合议庭 / 合議庭 majority with secret minority minutes
register.original_language_quote: 合议庭评议案件应当按照多数人的意见作出决定，少数人的意见应当记入笔录
register.secondary_quote: 合议庭评议案件，实行少数服从多数的原则
register.translation: When the collegiate panel deliberates a case it shall decide according to the majority opinion; the minority opinion shall be recorded in the minutes.

register.claim: Korean presidential decree names drafter/reviewer/cooperator/approver, 위임전결 and 대결. Same sequential-circulation family as 稟議. Only one captured rail (statute HTML); graded E3 and not cited as measured fact.
register.implementability_note: Operational decree, but one rail is E3.

register.claim: Art. 65 GG: the Federal Government as a collegium decides disagreements among ministers. Two rails, but this is collegial majority / cabinet decision — already in the English corpus as majority voting plus P52 nested councils. Not claimed as absent.
register.implementability_note: Majority collegial vote is already expressible.
register.original_language_quote: Über Meinungsverschiedenheiten zwischen den Bundesministern entscheidet die Bundesregierung
register.translation: The Federal Government decides disagreements among the Federal Ministers.

register.claim: Russian коллегиальность: joint discussion then either a college vote or a chair decision after consultation. Advisory form overlaps P58 owner-in-the-loop-stepwise; deciding form overlaps majority vote. Not claimed as absent.
register.original_language_quote: совместное обсуждение для принятия решения с учётом разных мнений и предложений
register.secondary_quote: посредством принятия решений по осуществлению поставленных управленческих задач группой должностных лиц
register.translation: joint discussion in order to take a decision taking different opinions and proposals into account
